reason: H0 follows the removed initializer protocol: it calls wuffs_gif__decoder__initialize and wuffs_zlib__decoder__initialize on uninitialized stack objects with arguments WUFFS_VERSION and 0. S1 instead exposes check_wuffs_version functions requiring WUFFS_VERSION and sizeof(*self), and those functions no longer memset the object. Consequently, H0 does not establish the required zeroed state or exercise the new version-and-structure-size validation protocol. This is material because decoder state includes status, coroutine suspension points, checksum state, and nested decoders.
evidence: gif_fuzzer.c declares wuffs_gif__decoder dec and immediately calls wuffs_gif__decoder__initialize(&dec, WUFFS_VERSION, 0), but S1 replaces that symbol with wuffs_gif__decoder__check_wuffs_version(wuffs_gif__decoder*, uint32_t, size_t).

zlib_fuzzer.c declares wuffs_zlib__decoder dec and immediately calls wuffs_zlib__decoder__initialize(&dec, WUFFS_VERSION, 0), but S1 replaces it with wuffs_zlib__decoder__check_wuffs_version(wuffs_zlib__decoder*, uint32_t, size_t).
S1's check_wuffs_version implementations reject either a mismatched WUFFS_VERSION or mismatched sizeof_star_self with ERROR_BAD_WUFFS_VERSION.
The removed initialize implementations conditionally called memset(self, 0, sizeof(*self)); the replacement check_wuffs_version implementations only set private_impl.magic after validation.
S1 explicitly adds wuffs_gif__lzw_decoder__reset, which performs memset before check_wuffs_version, demonstrating that reset/zeroing and version checking are now separate initialization steps.
recommended_action: Update both harnesses to zero-initialize their decoder objects and call the corresponding check_wuffs_version function with WUFFS_VERSION and sizeof(dec). Add a focused initialization-protocol target that varies wuffs_version, sizeof_star_self, and pre-initialization object bytes, verifies ERROR_BAD_WUFFS_VERSION for mismatches, and exercises valid initialization plus nested decoder/reset paths.
